name: Claude Code 2.1.224 — Self-Hosted Runner, Cross-Session Messaging, No Subagent Cap

name: ponytail — 98K Stars; Laziness Ladder Cuts Code 54–94%
hook: 98,100 stars for a Claude Code skill that enforces a 7-rung laziness ladder before writing a single line of custom code: stdlib first, native platform features second, existing dependencies third, one-liners before functions, and so on. Benchmarked at ~54% less code (range up to 94%), ~20% cheaper, and ~27% faster on real FastAPI + React sessions. Unlike caveman, which targets prose verbosity, ponytail targets code bloat while preserving security and accessibility guardrails.

name: JuliusBrussee/caveman — 96.7K Stars; Day 15; 65% Fewer Output Tokens
hook: Compresses agent responses into terse caveman-speak without losing technical accuracy — code, commands, and error messages remain byte-for-byte exact, only the prose is stripped. 65% average output token reduction (range 22–87% across 1,200 test scenarios). The `/caveman-compress` companion shrinks CLAUDE.md and other memory files by ~46%, saving input tokens on every future session permanently. Stack with headroom (input) and context-mode (session) for a full three-layer token budget.
recurring_note: ↑ Day 15 — 96.7K stars; canonical output-token compression tool

name: thedotmack/claude-mem — 90K Stars; Day 2; Persistent Context Across Sessions
hook: 90,000 stars. Captures everything Claude does across sessions, compresses with AI, and injects relevant context automatically into new sessions via lifecycle hooks — no manual context management. Three-layer progressive-disclosure architecture (search → timeline → fetch) cuts memory token overhead by ~10x vs naively injecting full history. Works with Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, and Gemini CLI.
